text:
arjun: scan-bot flagged a new SAST run as MISSING for repo infra-service - looks like the scanner couldn't fetch the commit results. CI shows a 403 from the scanner service account. tagging @maria and @davis.
maria: link?
arjun: https://ci.redwood/runs/5582 and SAST log snippet:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"accessDenied","serviceAccount":"scanner-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"}
```
davis: that SA's role was trimmed yesterday during RBAC cleanup (PR 2129). I removed roles/storage.objectViewer and repo read to follow least privilege.
arjun: scanner needs repo:packages/read and storage read to pull compiled artifacts. Without it the SAST harness marks the run as skipped and creates a failing guard in the security review board.
maria: this caused an automated block on the release candidate list for today. Can we prove the SA didn't use KMS keys to decrypt anything — product security asked for key access history.
ci-bot: build 2026-04-02T08:12Z used kms key projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ci/cryptoKeys/build-key for signing.
security-bot: to get KMS audit entries run:
```
gcloud logging read "protoPayload.serviceName=\"cloudkms.googleapis.com\" AND protoPayload.methodName:Decrypt AND resource.labels.key_ring=\"ci\" AND timestamp>\"2026-04-01T00:00:00Z\"" --limit 100
```
davis: I don't think the SA touched KMS. We removed its role to avoid accidental decrypts after last month’s incident. But need to confirm. I'll run the log query and attach to INFSEC-2205.
arjun: also we should add a premerge SAST gating check that fails the PR if the scanner run is skipped vs failed (false negatives). Right now the presubmit only looks for pass/fail, not 'missing'.
maria: agree. For short-term unblock: I can temporarily re-grant storage.objectViewer to scanner-sa in the infra IAM binding, deploy, re-run SAST, then remove the role with an audited change and a signed-off JIRA.
davis: instead of toggling permissions, could we give the CI pipeline a short-lived token with the exact permissions it needs? we already have a flow to mint ephemeral creds via KMS-wrapped service tokens.
arjun: that would be ideal. product security will want an audit trail for the token minting and for the KMS unwrap operation. We must ensure key usage is logged and alerts fire on unusual decrypts.
maria: I'll do the temporary grant to get the release unstuck and file INFSEC-2205 with steps: repro, patch PR, KMS logs, and recommended fix (ephemeral token via KMS + new presubmit check).
ci-bot: started rerun: https://ci.redwood/runs/5583 (scanner-sa regain permission).
scan-bot: SAST run 5583: 0 HIGH, 3 MED, 7 LOW (full report: https://scans.redwood/5583.json)
darvis: (typo) davis: thanks, looks green.
arjun: follow-ups: (1) add presubmit check for "scanner run status != MISSING" (2) implement ephemeral tokens for scanner (3) add KMS decrypt alert threshold for CI keys (4) update RBAC change playbook to include validating scanner access.
maria: I'll own (1) and (4). davis you take (2). security team (anya) can own (3) - tagging @anya in ticket.
davis: ack. I'll open a design RFC for ephemeral scanner creds referencing the keystore API.
security-bot: INFSEC-2205 created and linked to release blocker board. evidence: CI logs + KMS audit query command.
arjun: good. note for postmortem: root cause = overly aggressive RBAC prune left out scanner perms; contributory factor = presubmit didn't detect missing runs.
maria: adding a short blameless note to the release board and scheduling a 30-min sync tomorrow to triage automation gaps.
scan-bot: automated note: marking release candidate RC-2026-04-02 as unblocked.
arjun: thanks everyone, closing thread.
